findings.title: Unfiltered AF_VSOCK path from confined uids to the Windows host
findings.where: systemd/ossbot-gatekeeper.service, systemd/ossbot-sandboxd.service, Phase 2 runner/hermes unit templates; docs/VERIFICATION.md egress threat table
findings.detail: As uid hermes, AF_VSOCK connect to host CID 2 succeeds on ports 50000, 50002 and 50005. Hyper-V sockets bypass the iptables owner rules, the WSL NAT and the Hyper-V VM firewall, and no unit restricts address families. What the listeners are (possibly drvfs Plan 9 or the DNS tunnel) is not traced.
findings.action: Add RestrictAddressFamilies=AF_UNIX AF_INET AF_INET6 (+AF_NETLINK only if needed) to every non-root ossbot unit and the Phase 2 runner/hermes templates; assert it in tests/unit/test_systemd_units.py; probe vsock from the unit context (systemd-run with the same properties, unit Seccomp) and from each sandbox pool; add a threat-table row and ADR-0005 addendum; identify the host listeners and record any ADR-0007 impact.

findings.title: denied_dst special-purpose ranges
findings.action: Add 198.18.0.0/15 (fake-IP range of Windows VPN/proxy clients), 192.0.0.0/24, 224.0.0.0/4 and 240.0.0.0/4 to always_denied.cidrs.

findings.title: Host-listener probe too permissive
findings.action: In test_egress_surface.sh exempt only <NS>:53, and turn the loopback check into an explicit allowlist, since every service uid can reach any lo port.
